type: Yamato-class battleship (Kure Naval Arsenal; commissioned 16 Dec 1941)
schema_notes: level_m = deck height above design waterline (negative = below). confidence: sourced / typical / reconstruction (see mikasa.json).

basis.fact: Length 263 m overall (256 m waterline), beam 38.9 m, draught ~11 m
12 boilers, 4 steam turbines, 4 shafts, 150,000 shp, 27 kt
Complement 3,233 (design); 3,332 aboard at the final sortie, of whom ~3,056 died
9 x Type 94 46 cm guns in 3 triple turrets; each turret 2,774 t; each gun 162 t
Main belt 41 cm over the citadel, lower belt 28 cm protecting the magazines; turret face ~65 cm
Turret face armour 25 in (~64 cm), the heaviest ever fitted; total armour ~23,000 t; bridge top rangefinder ~100 ft (30 m) above the deck
Yamato Museum 1/10 model: 26.3 m long, 3.9 m wide, reconstructed from drawings, dive-survey footage and crew testimony
7 Apr 1945: at least 11 torpedoes (most on the port side) and 6+ bombs hit
Starboard engine and boiler rooms were counter-flooded to correct the port list (~13:33), drowning the men at their stations; capsized ~14:20; magazine explosion ~14:23 (which magazine is disputed)

displacement_t.confidence: typical (widely cited; not verified this session)

flooding.watertight_subdivision: Extremely subdivided: the common figure is 1,147 watertight compartments (1,065 below the armour deck). The armoured citadel covers the magazines and machinery over roughly the middle half of the waterline length.
flooding.watertight_confidence: typical (widely cited; not verified this session)
flooding.torpedo_defence: Inclined belt with a liquid-loaded side protection system; the joint between the upper and lower belt was a known weak point (typical)
flooding.pumps: Electric drainage pumps; counter-flooding system with remote-controlled valves to correct list (sourced in effect, through the 1945 counter-flooding)
flooding.sea_cocks: Counter-flooding valves to the outboard voids and the starboard machinery rooms; magazine sprinkler and flooding systems

sequence: 12:32 first air attack wave; bombs aft
Torpedoes concentrated on the port side cause a growing port list
~13:33 starboard engine and boiler rooms counter-flooded to correct the list, drowning the engineering crews
~14:23 magazine explosion (fore No.1/2 or aft secondary, disputed); mushroom cloud
Wreck in two main pieces at ~340 m depth (typical figure)

game_sinking_hooks: List meter: port flooding raises the list; the player can open starboard counter-flooding valves (trading engine power for stability)
Above ~20 degrees list, magazine shells shift inside the turret: explosion risk while capsizing
Many small compartments: slow progressive flooding along the damaged side

uncertain: Bridge tower level heights are approximate; the tower had ~13 levels and the game uses 4 representative levels.
1,147-compartment figure, displacement figures and wreck depth are widely cited but were not verified in this session.
Hammock vs bunk mix in the berthing.
